To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
estrogen does not affect the growth of normal mammary cells in vitro and that phenol red does not mask any estrogenic effect.

the pH indicator phenol red, present in most culture media, does not influence the growth of normal or malignant human and rodent mammary cells in response to hormones and growth factors and that the antiestrogen, keoxifense, also does not influence the proliferation of mammary cells in vitro.
phenol red has no effect on the growth of primary cultures of human, mouse, or rat mammary cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the growth of normal and neoplastic human mammary cells in vitro.
the growth of normal and neoplastic breast epithelium.
the growth of normal and neoplastic human and rodent mammary cells in serum-free primary culture.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the growth of normal and neoplastic human, mouse, or rat mammary cells is not affected by phenol red, E2, or keoxifene.
phenol red and estradiol have little or no effect on the growth of human and rodent normal mammary cells in vitro.
the growth of normal and neoplastic human, mouse, or rat mammary cells does not appear to be directly regulated by estrogens in primary culture.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
phenol red does not affect growth and is not a weak estrogen, and that the lack of response of normal mammary cells to E2 in primary culture is not an artifact of the culture conditions.
phenol red and E2 do not affect growth of normal or neoplastic mamary cells in primary culture.
the lack of an estrogenic response of normal mammary cells in vitro may be due to the lack of an appropriate estrogenic signal in vivo.
The main takeaway from our work is that
phenol red does not mask the effect of E2 in these primary cultures.
, in contrast to what has been reported for some tumor lines, the growth of normal mammary cells is not stimulated by E2 in vitro.
phenol red does not affect the growth response of normal or neoplastic mammy cells in culture.
